program: SNAP — Arkansas has no distinctive local program nickname; this pack found no distinctive branded EBT card name either (see PROVENANCE.md Finding 5)
agency: Arkansas Department of Human Services (DHS), Division of County Operations (DCO)
admin_note: Arkansas is a STATE-ADMINISTERED SNAP program run by DHS's Division of County Operations through county DHS offices — not independent county agencies like CA/NY/MN/WI/VA. GENUINE STRUCTURAL FLAGSHIP FINDING this pack found: Arkansas Code § 20-76-115, added by Act 675 of 2023 (SB306), STATUTORILY BARS DHS from adopting income-based broad-based categorical eligibility (raising the gross income standard above the plain federal 130% FPL, 7 U.S.C. § 2014(c)) UNLESS DHS separately obtains a federal BBCE waiver from USDA FNS — and, independently, caps any RESOURCE-based categorical-eligibility exemption to a TEMPORARY $5,500 asset limit for up to twelve (12) months once every five (5) years, not a permanent resource-test removal, per DHS's own April 2025 emergency-rule filing implementing the Act (see PROVENANCE.md Finding 1). This is a legislative self-restriction on the agency's own eligibility policy, structurally similar in KIND (though different in subject) to this roster's Oklahoma finding (statutory ABAWD-waiver-request ban) and Arkansas's own separate ABAWD finding below. SEPARATELY, this pack found the Arkansas SNAP Certification Manual's own ABAWD age-exemption table (SNAP Manual dated 01/01/2024) still reflects only the 2023 Fiscal Responsibility Act's PRE-OBBBA incremental schedule, topping out at exempt-at-55 (i.e., subject through age 54) — with NO mention anywhere in the manual of OBBBA's true current federal standard, 18-64, effective immediately upon its July 4, 2025 enactment (see PROVENANCE.md Finding 2). ALSO found: the manual's own ABAWD-waiver-status section (SNAP 3501) is dated 'SNAP Manual 01/01/17' — unrevised for roughly nine years despite the manual's front matter showing a 07/01/2026 revision date — and states plainly Arkansas is 'currently not under a waiver' as of that stale 2017 revision (see PROVENANCE.md Finding 3). Confirm current operative practice with the applicant's own local DHS county office, the same caution this roster already carries for CA/NY/MN/WI/OH/NC/NJ/VA/GA/IN/TN/MO/MD/CO/SC/AL/LA/KY/OK.
system: DHS's Division of County Operations processes SNAP; applicants apply online through Access Arkansas (access.arkansas.gov), by mail, by fax, or in person at a local DHS county office. The normal processing standard is no later than 30 calendar days from the date a valid application is filed (SNAP Manual § 8500); expedited service (households with very low income and liquid resources, or destitute migrant/seasonal farmworkers) is the plain federal 7 calendar days (SNAP Manual § 9100) — Arkansas does not shorten this the way this roster's Kentucky pack found Kentucky does (5 days). An interview is generally required, in person or by phone.

verification.method: Direct WebFetch retrieval of DHS's own official SNAP Certification Manual PDF (humanservices.arkansas.gov, 4.8MB, converted with pdftotext -layout) and DHS's own Appendix D/Exhibits A-B dollar-figure PDF (SNAP-Appendices-10.01.2025.pdf, effective 10/1/2025, current FFY2026 figures) — both read via WebFetch after direct curl with a browser User-Agent returned a clean HTTP 403 on every DHS host attempted (see PROVENANCE.md Finding 0). Also directly curl-fetched (clean HTTP 200, no barrier): the Arkansas Bureau of Legislative Research's own emergency-rule filing implementing Act 675 of 2023, which reproduces the Act's own enacted bill text (Senate Bill 306, 94th General Assembly) in full — read directly for its statutory language, not inferred from a secondary summary. USDA FNS's current Restaurant Meals Program state list was fetched directly (clean HTTP 200, Arkansas absent). WebSearch cross-checks located FindLaw's current-code mirror of Arkansas Code § 20-76-409 (Opt out), independently confirming Arkansas's full drug-felony opt-out, cross-checked against the SNAP Certification Manual's own current disqualification-category list (no drug-felony category found).
verification.gates: Every DHS-hosted PDF this pack attempted (the full SNAP Certification Manual, the Appendix D/Exhibits dollar-figure PDF, and the separate SNAP Policy Directives change-history PDF) returned a clean HTTP 403 to direct curl with a browser User-Agent on every attempt — a genuine, disclosed access barrier for Arkansas's PRIMARY policy-manual publisher. This pack resolved it by fetching the SAME PDFs through WebFetch instead, which retrieved each document's full binary content successfully (the manual PDF: 4.8MB; the appendices PDF: 1.2MB) for direct pdftotext extraction — a genuine, disclosed access-barrier workaround using a different fetch path to the SAME primary-source file, not a substitution of a different or lower-quality source. Justia's Arkansas Code mirror (law.justia.com) also 403'd on direct WebFetch, the now-familiar Justia-block pattern this roster has documented repeatedly (Louisiana, Virginia, Indiana, Missouri, Maryland, Colorado, South Carolina, Alabama, Kentucky, Oklahoma) — resolved via FindLaw's current-code mirror instead, which returned readable text cleanly. By contrast, the Arkansas Bureau of Legislative Research's own emergency-rule filing (arkleg.state.ar.us) returned a clean HTTP 200 to direct curl with no barrier at all.
